subject: Pilot credits phasing & data egress sensitivity for vendor swap
messages:
From: Amit Shah <amit.shah@novamed.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Chen <laura.chen@novamed.com>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Exploring a swap to Redwood + pricing ask

Hi Monica —

Thanks again for the call last week. We ran the numbers and the move off our current provider is still feasible if we can get a competitive package that covers: (1) initial pilot credits to offset first-month token volume, (2) a clear egress credit schedule (we have ~100 TB of historical data to move), and (3) help on the first 6 weeks of runbook/onboarding to reduce ops risk.

Quick context: Novamed is forecasting ~5M generated tokens/day in steady state (peak 8M) and ~200k embedding ops/week during the pilot. We care about predictable per-token economics but also about the one-time migration costs that typically block an executive sign-off.

Two asks I wanted on paper so our procurement team can compare apples-to-apples: a) a buyout number (one-time) that offsets 90 days of migration friction + egress; and b) an alternative phased credit plan that reduces cash outlay but gives us runway to validate performance.

Also, with SOC2 in our security checklist, please point me to your most recent attestation or related summary.

If easier, can you propose a single-sheet offer we can present to procurement?

—Amit

--
Amit Shah
VP Product & Ops, Novamed
amit.shah@novamed.com

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring a swap to Redwood + pricing ask

Amit —

Appreciate the clear asks. I pulled together two practical options that typically win procurement approval: a Pilot-Credit Phasing plan (lower up-front cash, staged credits) and a single buyout number (one-time payment, no credits). I've summarized both below and attached a migration workbook / preliminary SOW. Full workbook attached: novamed_migration_workbook.xlsx.

Option A — Pilot Credit Phasing (recommended for rapid validation)
- Month 0 (pilot kickoff, Weeks 0–4): 100% token credits up to 2.5M tokens/day (covers pilot spikes), plus 50TB egress credit for bulk transfer.
- Month 1: 70% token credit up to 3.5M tokens/day, 20TB egress credit.
- Month 2: 40% token credit up to 5M tokens/day, no additional egress credit.
- Onboarding: 3 days of SRE-led migration support + 5 days of engineering office-hours (remote); we can expand for professional services but included baseline is intended to remove first-week ops friction.

Option B — One-time Buyout
- One-time credit: $150,000 payable at signature. Covers expected migration engineering and egress offsets (we estimate >50 TB paid conversion).
- Standard per-token pricing thereafter (we'll put the exact per-token tiers into the formal quote).

Egress economics (sensitivity) — our default treatment and optional protections
- We will provide an initial pool of egress credits as above for bulk transfer. After credit pool is exhausted, egress billed at $0.02/GB (US regions) unless we agree a fixed buyout.
- If long tail of egress remains, we can add a time-limited per-GB cap for first 90 days to provide predictability; we typically structure that as a capped pass-through with an escape clause if volumes exceed 3x expected.

KPIs / Acceptance criteria we recommend Novamed include in the decision package
- Onboarding completed (data and model compatibility validation) within 6 weeks of kick-off.
- P50 latency of core generate endpoint < 300ms in the target region.
- 99.9% uptime for production routes in first 90 days.
- Token spend within 15% of forecast after month-2 ramp.

Attachments: migration workbook (workbook has a line-by-line runbook + egress estimate). I'll also attach a short SOW draft (SOW-Redwood-migration-v1.2.pdf) that outlines deliverables and a baseline professional-services statement. SOC2 summary attached as soc2_redwood_summary.pdf.

Next steps I'd propose:
1) You confirm whether the Pilot Credit Phasing or Buyout is preferred.
2) We lock in the pilot dates — I recommend a tech kickoff the week of May 24 to hit your target timeline.
3) Marissa will spin up the formal quote & DocuSign if you select Option A or B.

If helpful I can also include an explicit per-token table (hourly/hourly-equivalent) but wanted to get the high-level tradeoffs on paper first.

Thanks — talk soon.

—Monica

Monica Patel

monica_patel@redwood.ai | +1 650-555-0147
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@novamed.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amit Shah <amit.shah@novamed.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring a swap to Redwood + pricing ask

Monica —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the workbook — that looks helpful. A few clarifying items from procurement and engineering before we present to finance: 

1) Can the pilot credits be scoped per "metering group"? We need to guarantee credits for the clinical inference pipeline separately from non-clinical tooling.
2) For the egress credits: that 50TB bulk credit is most of our hot-data transfer, but we'll likely have an additional 20–30 TB in slower archival exports. Can you confirm whether archival exports are treated at the same $0.02/GB after credits?
3) SOC2 — the summary is good, but procurement wants the most recent cert date and scope (subservice orgs). Is that in the PDF or a carrier link?
4) Does the migration require app-level SDK changes, or can we point our runtime at an API-compatible endpoint with minimal code change? Our dev team wants to understand if there's a 2–3 week code integration or if it's a config switch.

Two asks from my side: please split the initial workbook into the two metering groups (clinical vs non-clinical) and include a simple per-group cost delta. Also, iterate the SOW to explicitly list who from Redwood will own the runbook tasks vs our internal list.

If you can get a revised workbook and SOW by EOD Wed (May 6), we can bring this to our procurement committee on May 10.

—Laura

--
Laura Chen
Director, Engineering Operations, Novamed
laura.chen@novamed.com
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@novamed.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 6 May 2026 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring a swap to Redwood + pricing ask

Laura / Amit —

Thanks — all good asks. Quick answers and next steps below; I've updated the workbook and SOW and attached the revised files. 

Short answers:
- Metering groups: yes. We'll split the pilot credits across two metering groups (clinical pipeline gets first priority credits). I've flagged the workbook with a per-group credit allocation (clinical = 65% of token credits during Month 0, non-clinical = 35%).
- Archival exports: archival exports are billed at the same post-credit per-GB rate ($0.02/GB) unless you pick the buyout option, in which case the one-time amount absorbs the archive delta (we estimated archival egress at ~25 TB).
- SOC2: the attached PDF includes the latest attestation date (2026-04-12) and scope; link in the workbook points to the cert repository if you need the full report (we can share an IAW NDA if required).
- Integration effort: for most Novamed use-cases we can keep changes to configuration and small SDK toggles — no app-level rewrite expected. Typical integration is 1–3 sprints (2–6 weeks) depending on embedding integration. We put a conservative 3-week dev integration buffer in the SOW.

Attached: revised migration workbook (novamed_migration_workbook.xlsx), revised SOW (SOW-Redwood-migration-v1.2.pdf), SOC2 summary (soc2_redwood_summary.pdf).

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Confirm pathway: Pilot Credit Phasing vs $150k buyout by EOD Fri May 7.
2) If Pilot selected, we will: a) issue an updated formal quote & DocuSign (Marissa), b) schedule tech kickoff — suggested dates May 24–28, c) Karthik will own the technical runbook pairing calls.
3) Please share Novamed's list of participants for the kickoff (Eng manager, SRE, security lead).

I'll also include a short one-page callout for procurement that highlights the two options and the upside for staging credits (lower initial cash, ability to validate infra/latency before committing to full consumption).

If you want, I can jump on a 30-min call tomorrow to walk procurement through the one-pager.

—Monica
